protocol: Labels, predictions and the bar rule were written and committed before any decider call on these cases.

The decider request is core.mjs verdictRequest (v1, unchanged since round 1). The rules and the bar are core.mjs ruleVerdict and applyBar with RULE_DEFAULTS and ROLE_BUDGET_MIN, the same code the live gate runs.
Step 1: run the 8 tune cases. Step 2: fix the bar by the rule below and commit it as STAY_QUIET_BAR in core.mjs. Step 3: run the 22 held cases once.

Bar rule. Use only tune cases that no rule catches. A is the set of their stay_quiet probabilities where wake_pm or tell_mason is expected, and H is the set where stay_quiet is expected. If min(H) - 0.01 > max(A), the bar is min(H) - 0.01, rounded down to 2 decimals: the highest bar with no needless wake on the tune cases. Otherwise alarms win, and the bar is max(A) + 0.01, rounded up to 2 decimals. Cap it at 0.99.
Report two confusion tables on the held cases: the whole gate (rules, then the decider with the bar) and the decider alone (its top choice). Name the layer that decided each case.

predictions.stall rule: Catches the held stalls that are running past their budget: s3-run-default, s3-estimate, s3-charter. Misses s3-loop, whose retry loop keeps the quiet time short. Does not fire on h3-estimate-long or h3-eval.
predictions.promise rule: Catches s3-promise. Wakes the PM needlessly on f3-promise-phrase, whose finished reply says it will report back only if something changes. Does not catch s3-ci-wait, whose wording is not a promise phrase.
predictions.question rule: Catches w3-card-old. Catches m3-card-token but routes it to wake_pm, the wrong recipient, since the rule always wakes the PM. w3-card-new is below the timeout and goes to the decider.
predictions.bar: Guess: the bar lands between 0.85 and 0.94. If so, it turns unsure stay_quiet answers on w3-card-new and m3-owner into wakes, and wakes no alarming-reply case, since round 2 gave those 0.94 or more.
predictions.whole gate: Guess: at least 17 of the 22 held cases right, with at most 1 missed alarm.
predictions.decider alone: Guess: about 14 of 22, with every stall that the rules catch counted as a missed alarm.
